title: Collective variables for homophily-driven network rewiring dynamics
summary: Stochastic network rewiring processes, in which edges dynamically rewire based on fixed node attributes, are widely used in applications ranging from social dynamics to neuroscience and form an important component of adaptive network modelling. In this paper, we identify low-dimensional collective variables (CVs) that capture the essential macroscopic behavior of such time-evolving networks and enable reduced-order descriptions of their dynamics.
